### Step 1: run Plink on the filtered SNP dataset to quantify pairwise relatedness among all samples in the dataset. I did this on the UCLA cluster with the following job script:
```{bash, eval=FALSE}
#### submit_job.sh START ####
#!/bin/bash
#$ -cwd
#$ -o ./joblog.$JOB_ID.txt                   #set the job log output file
#$ -j y                                      #set error = Merged with joblog
#$ -l h_rt=1:00:00,h_data=3G      #specify requested resources (h_rt gives time request in 'hrs:mins:secs' format) (h_data specifies requested RAM per task) (highp=TRUE means run it on Aguillon Lab owned nodes)
#$ -pe shared 1                              #specify number of CPUs requested

#load necessary modules
. /u/local/Modules/default/init/modules.sh

#run plink2 (v2.0.0) to make 'KING' relatedness table
/u/project/aguillon/shared_bin/plink2 --vcf final.trimmed.snps.vcf --make-king-table
```

### Step 2: Read in Plink table to this R session and visualize
```{r}
#load packages
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)

#read in data
x<-read.table("~/Desktop/2026.eagle.mountain/plink2.kin0")

#visualize data
hist(x$V6, breaks=100, xlim = c(-0.5,0.5))
#are there any individuals more related than expected by chance in a wild pop (i.e., > 0)
hist(x$V6, breaks=100, xlim = c(0,0.5))

#convert the plink table into a matrix for plotting
rev_comp <- x
rev_comp$V1 <- x$V2
rev_comp$V2 <- x$V1
full_comp <- rbind(x, rev_comp)
full_comp<-full_comp[,c(1,2,6)]
# Include diagonal (self comparisons)
items <- unique(c(x$V1, x$V2))
diag_df <- data.frame(V1 = items, V2 = items, V6 = 1)
full_comp <- rbind(full_comp, diag_df)
# Create matrix
mat <- dcast(full_comp, V1 ~ V2, value.var = "V6")
rownames(mat) <- mat$V1
mat <- mat[,-1]  # remove redundant column
mat <- as.matrix(mat)

#make heatmap
heatmap(mat, Rowv = NA, Colv = NA, scale = "none", col = heat.colors(256))

# Melt for ggplot
melted <- melt(mat)

ggplot(melted, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("black","grey","red"), values = c(0,.83,1),limits=c(-2.5,0.5))+
  theme_bw()+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust=1))+
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value,2)), color = "black", size = 2)

```
